blogs.title: Teaching AI New Image Tricks Without Making It Forget: A Simple Guide to Orthogonal Finetuning
blogs.description: This post explains the paper’s core idea in plain language: how Orthogonal Finetuning helps text-to-image models learn new tasks without damaging the image quality and semantics they learned during pretraining. It would introduce the problem of finetuning diffusion models, why models often 'forget' or collapse, and how rotating weights instead of freely changing them can preserve what the model already knows.

blogs.title: Why Angles Matter More Than Weight Size in AI Image Generation
blogs.description: This post focuses on the paper’s main intuition that semantic meaning in neural networks is strongly tied to the direction, or angle, of neurons rather than just their raw magnitude. It would break down ideas like hyperspherical energy, pairwise neuron relationships, and why preserving these geometric structures can help keep a model’s visual understanding intact during finetuning.

blogs.title: OFT vs LoRA vs DreamBooth vs ControlNet: What’s the Best Way to Customize a Diffusion Model?
blogs.description: This post compares Orthogonal Finetuning with popular adaptation methods such as LoRA, DreamBooth, and ControlNet. It would explain how each method changes a pretrained model, what tradeoffs they make in speed, stability, parameter count, and quality, and why OFT stands out in the paper for converging faster and preserving subject identity and controllability better.

blogs.title: From Personalized Avatars to Sketch-Guided Images: Where Orthogonal Finetuning Shines
blogs.description: This post highlights the practical use cases explored in the paper, especially subject-driven generation and controllable generation. It would show how OFT helps generate consistent images of a person or object from a few example photos, and how it improves image generation from control signals like edges, segmentation maps, and landmarks.

blogs.title: A Smarter Way to Fine-Tune Diffusion Models: Inside COFT and the Stability Problem
blogs.description: This post zooms in on Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT), the paper’s more stable version of OFT. It would explain why even a good finetuning method can become too flexible, how COFT adds a constraint to keep updates close to the original model, and why that makes training more predictable and easier to tune in real-world workflows.
